column2: State the main subject or focus of the lesson. This should be a concise phrase or sentence that clearly identifies what the lesson is about. It provides a quick reference point for the content area being covered and helps align the lesson within a broader unit of work or curriculum area.

Identify the key facts, concepts, or understandings that students are expected to learn. This includes subject-specific information, terms, or principles that form the foundation of the lesson. Focus on what students need to know in order to develop deeper understanding or apply skills effectively.

Describe the specific abilities or processes students will develop or practice in the lesson. These may include thinking, practical, or subject-specific skills (e.g., analysing, measuring, writing, coding). Focus on what students should be able to do by the end of the lesson, either independently or with guidance.
